dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps the seven real inputs to alpha*epsilonC + beta*epsilonB + beta*ug + lambda*epsilonX.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the scalar upper bound on the right-hand side of the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forms the vector indexed by Fin n whose coordinate i is alpha*computationError(i) + beta*rhsError(i) + beta*gmresError(i) + lambda*solutionError(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the weighted sum of the four error vectors whose Euclidean norm appears on the left-hand side of the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a vector x : Fin n -> Real, returns sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of x(i)^2), its Euclidean 2-norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses all four assumed vector-norm bounds and the norm bounded in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Adds two vectors pointwise: the coordinate at i is x(i) + y(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the four scaled error vectors in LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Multiplies a vector pointwise by a real scalar: the coordinate at i is a*x(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It scales the error vectors by alpha, beta, beta, and lambda in LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: Returns the finite sum of squared coordinates, sum over i in Fin n of x(i)^2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the squared Euclidean norm under the square root in LocalDef003.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type with exactly n indices, conventionally represented by natural numbers less than n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each error object an n-dimensional real vector and determines the indices included in every norm.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero

binders: An arbitrary natural number n, which may be zero.
Arbitrary real numbers alpha, beta, lambda, epsilonC, epsilonB, ug, and epsilonX.
Arbitrary functions computationError, rhsError, gmresError, and solutionError from Fin n to Real, viewed as four n-dimensional real vectors.
hypotheses: The Euclidean norm of computationError is at most epsilonC.
The Euclidean norm of rhsError is at most epsilonB.
The Euclidean norm of gmresError is at most ug.
The Euclidean norm of solutionError is at most epsilonX.
conclusions: The Euclidean norm of alpha*computationError + beta*rhsError + beta*gmresError + lambda*solutionError is at most alpha*epsilonC + beta*epsilonB + beta*ug + lambda*epsilonX.
mathematical_definitions: For x : Fin n -> Real, ||x||_2 means sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of x(i)^2).
Vector addition and scalar multiplication are pointwise.
The combined vector E is defined by E(i) = alpha*computationError(i) + beta*rhsError(i) + beta*gmresError(i) + lambda*solutionError(i).
The scalar bound B is alpha*epsilonC + beta*epsilonB + beta*ug + lambda*epsilonX.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension n, every choice of real coefficients and bounds, and every four real vectors of dimension n, if alpha, beta, and lambda are nonnegative and the four vectors have Euclidean norms bounded respectively by epsilonC, epsilonB, ug, and epsilonX, then the Euclidean norm of their weighted sum alpha*computationError + beta*rhsError + beta*gmresError + lambda*solutionError is at most alpha*epsilonC + beta*epsilonB + beta*ug + lambda*epsilonX.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n is unrestricted and includes n = 0. In that case Fin n is empty, every displayed norm is zero, and the proposition contains no coordinate-level information.
The coefficients alpha, beta, and lambda are required only to be nonnegative; they need not be strictly positive.
The same coefficient beta weights both rhsError and gmresError, and the same beta appears on their two upper-bound terms.
The bounds epsilonC, epsilonB, ug, and epsilonX have no separate nonnegativity hypotheses, although each norm-bound hypothesis forces its corresponding bound to be nonnegative.
Because the statement is a chain of implications, it is vacuously true whenever any listed hypothesis is false.
The four vectors are otherwise arbitrary and need not satisfy independence, orthogonality, componentwise bounds, or any structural relation.
The proposition asserts only an aggregate Euclidean-norm upper bound. It does not assert equality, sharpness, componentwise error control, relative error control, or the existence of witnesses.
The names computationError, rhsError, gmresError, and solutionError encode no formal computational, algorithmic, matrix, or exact-solution semantics.
